title: Yokai of Japan
subtitle: A Japanese Folklore Coloring Book of 50 Monsters for Adults and Teens, with Lore and Profile Cards
description:
Japan has the richest supernatural tradition in the world. This illustrated bestiary brings fifty of its monsters together, including Oni, Kitsune, Tengu, Kappa and Gashadokuro. Each one is drawn from primary sources and yours to color.

Every creature gets four pages. A profile card gives the name in English and Japanese kanji, with its type, domain and three defining attributes. A lore page draws on the Kojiki, Toriyama Sekien's Gazu Hyakki Yagyo, the Heike Monogatari and Lafcadio Hearn's Kwaidan. It faces a full-page illustration in detailed monochrome line art at adult complexity.

A blank backing page follows each illustration so color bleeds nowhere. Pencils, fine liners and crayons all work. Alcohol markers work too, on the blank page behind.

title: Vættir of the Norse Eddas
subtitle: A Nordic Folklore Coloring Book of 50 Monsters for Adults and Teens, with Lore and Profile Cards
description:
The real creatures behind the myths, illustrated and yours to color. This bestiary gives you fifty beings from Norse and Scandinavian mythology, including Draugr, Fenrir and Jörmungandr. Each one is drawn from the original Eddas and sagas.

Every creature gets four pages. A profile card gives the Old Norse name, the Younger Futhark runic name, type, domain, nature and three sourced attributes. A lore page draws on the Prose Edda, the Poetic Edda, the Vǫlsunga Saga and the Grettis Saga. It faces a full-page black-and-white illustration made for adult coloring.

A blank backing page sits behind every illustration to protect the next page. Colored pencils and crayons are recommended. Alcohol markers may bleed.

title: Birds of India
subtitle: Colour Your Way Through India's Feathered World
description:
India is home to over 1,300 bird species. This revised edition brings 50 of the most spectacular to your coloring table, from the Indian Peacock and the Himalayan Monal to the Great Hornbill and the critically endangered Great Indian Bustard.

Every page features one bird drawn in the style of a classic ornithological field guide. The lines are bold, the anatomy is accurate and there is room to color. Each page carries the common name, the scientific name and a fun fact. A full index lists all 50 birds.

Each illustration has its own page with a blank page behind it. Colored pencils, crayons and gel pens all work well. Alcohol markers may bleed through. Part of the Birds of the World series, for children and adults who love birds.

title: Birds of Brazil
subtitle: Coloring Book for Kids with 50 Illustrations, Scientific Names and Fun Facts
description:
Brazil has more bird species than any other country, over 1,900 in all. This expanded second edition brings 50 of the most spectacular to your coloring table, from the Hyacinth Macaw and the Toco Toucan to the Paradise Tanager and the Guianan Cock-of-the-rock.

Every page features one bird drawn in the style of an ornithological engraving. The lines are bold, the anatomy is accurate and there is room to color. Each page carries the common name, the scientific name and a fun fact. An illustrated index lists all 50 birds.

Each illustration is printed on one side only, with a blank reverse. Colored pencils, crayons and gel pens are recommended. Alcohol markers may bleed. Volume 2 of the Birds of the World series.

title: Birds of Costa Rica
subtitle: Coloring Book for Kids with 50 Illustrations, Scientific Names and Fun Facts
description:
Costa Rica has more than 900 bird species in a country smaller than West Virginia. This expanded second edition brings 50 of the most spectacular to your child's coloring table, from the Resplendent Quetzal and the Keel-billed Toucan to the Sunbittern and the Three-wattled Bellbird.

Every page features one bird drawn in the style of a classic ornithological field guide. The lines are bold, the anatomy is accurate and there is room to color. Each page carries the common name, the scientific name and a fun fact. The book includes the national bird, the Clay-colored Thrush.

Each illustration has its own page with a blank reverse, so colors never bleed through. Any coloring medium works, including markers. Volume 3 of the Birds of the World series, ideal for children aged 6 to 9.

title: Birds of Madagascar
subtitle: Coloring Book for Kids with 50 Illustrations, Scientific Names and Fun Facts
description:
Madagascar split from Africa 160 million years ago, and over 100 of its bird species exist nowhere else. This book brings 50 of the most extraordinary to your coloring table, from the Helmet Vanga to the rare Madagascar Fish Eagle and the Long-tailed Ground-roller.

Every page features one species drawn in the style of a classic ornithological engraving. The lines are bold, the anatomy is accurate and there is room to color. Each page carries the common name, the scientific name and a fun fact. A full index lists all 50 birds.

Each illustration has its own page with a blank page behind it. Colored pencils, crayons and gel pens all work well. Alcohol markers may bleed through. Part of the Birds of the World series.
